assertion_results.text: Data extraction correctly identifies CVE-2026-31812, library quinn-proto, affected range < 0.11.14, and fixed version 0.11.14 from the Vulnerability issue (Step 1)
assertion_results.evidence: In data-extraction.md, the Step 1 table lists: CVE ID = CVE-2026-31812, Vulnerable library = quinn-proto, Affected version range = 'versions before 0.11.14', Fixed version = 0.11.14. All four fields are correctly extracted.

assertion_results.text: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as Cargo based on the library name and component context (Step 1 Ecosystem detection)
assertion_results.evidence: In data-extraction.md, the Ecosystem Detection section states: 'Vulnerable library: quinn-proto (Rust crate)', 'Ecosystem: Cargo', 'Category: Source dependency', 'Lock file: Cargo.lock'. The ecosystem is correctly identified as Cargo.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the security-matrix.md supportability matrix — no versions are skipped (Important Rule 4)
assertion_results.evidence: In version-impact.md, the Version Impact table includes all 7 versions from the matrix: 2.1.0, 2.1.1 (stream 2.1.x), 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 2.2.4 (stream 2.2.x). The security-matrix-mock.md defines exactly these 7 versions across both streams. No versions are skipped.

assertion_results.text: Version impact analysis uses pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version, not branch HEAD (Important Rule 13)
assertion_results.evidence: In version-impact.md, the Evidence section states 'Lock file versions extracted via git show <tag>:Cargo.lock for each pinned backend commit' and lists tags v0.3.8, v0.3.12, v0.4.5, v0.4.8, v0.4.9, v0.4.11, v0.4.12 — matching the pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix columns in security-matrix-mock.md. No branch HEAD references are used.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table identifies retag versions and carries forward the affected status from the original version (Important Rule 5)
assertion_results.evidence: In version-impact.md, version 2.2.2 row shows: quinn-proto = 0.11.12, Affected = YES, Notes = 'retag of 2.2.1 (same as 2.2.1)'. The Evidence section shows 'v0.4.9 | _(retag of v0.4.8)_ | skipped -- same source as v0.4.8'. The retag is identified and the affected status (YES) is carried forward from the original version 2.2.1.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction proposes replacing PSIRT-assigned versions with lock-file-verified versions, showing the diff (Step 3.2)
assertion_results.evidence: In affects-versions.md, the 'Current vs Proposed Affects Versions' table shows: Current (PSIRT-assigned) = 'RHTPA 2.0.0', Proposed (from lock file analysis) = 'RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2'. The Comment section shows the diff: 'Corrected Affects Versions: [RHTPA 2.0.0] --> [RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2].' The correction rationale explains why RHTPA 2.0.0 is incorrect.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction references version names from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6)
assertion_results.evidence: In affects-versions.md, the proposed versions are referenced by name: 'RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2'. The Jira Update section uses placeholder IDs '<jira-id-for-RHTPA-2.2.0>' etc., and explicitly states 'Version IDs are discovered dynamically via getJiraIssueTypeMetaWithFields (Step 3.1), not hardcoded.' No hardcoded numeric Jira version IDs appear anywhere in the file.

assertion_results.text: Remediation tasks include Repository, Target Branch, acceptance criteria, and dependency linkage between upstream and downstream tasks (Important Rule 9)
assertion_results.evidence: In remediation.md: Task 1 (Upstream Backport) includes Repository = 'backend', Target Branch = 'release/0.4.z', Acceptance Criteria with 3 checkboxes, and Link = 'Depend (TC-8001 --> this task)'. Task 2 (Downstream Propagation) includes Repository = 'rhtpa-release.0.4.z', Target Branch = 'main', Acceptance Criteria with 2 checkboxes, and Dependencies including '<upstream-backport-task-key> (upstream backport must merge first)' plus 'Blocks (upstream backport task --> this task)' link.

assertion_results.text: For Cargo ecosystem, remediation creates two tasks: upstream backport task and downstream propagation subtask with Blocks dependency (Important Rule 8)
assertion_results.evidence: In remediation.md, for the 2.2.x stream (within issue scope): Task 1 = 'Upstream Backport (2.2.x)' with summary 'Remediate CVE-2026-31812: bump quinn-proto to 0.11.14 (rhtpa-2.2)', Task 2 = 'Downstream Propagation (2.2.x)' with summary 'Propagate CVE-2026-31812 fix: update backend ref in rhtpa-release.0.4.z (rhtpa-2.2)'. Task 2 Links section includes 'Blocks (upstream backport task --> this task)'. Exactly two tasks with Blocks dependency.

assertion_results.text: The analysis presents triage recommendations as proposed actions — framing Affects Versions changes, label additions, and status transitions as proposals rather than executed mutations (Guardrails)
assertion_results.evidence: In affects-versions.md: 'After engineer confirmation, the Affects Versions field would be updated' and 'A correction comment would be posted to TC-8001' — conditional 'would be' language indicating proposals, not executed mutations. In remediation.md: 'The following comment would be posted to TC-8001' — proposal language. Remediation tasks are described with what they contain, not stated as having been created. The Jira update code block uses placeholder IDs indicating it has not been executed.

assertion_results.text: The data-extraction output describes Step 0.7 actions before the Step 1 data table: assigning the CVE issue to the current user and transitioning it to Assigned status (Step 0.7)
assertion_results.evidence: In data-extraction.md, the file begins with '# Step 0.7 -- Assign and Transition to Assigned' (line 1), which describes: (1) retrieving current user's Jira account ID via jira.user_info(), (2) assigning TC-8001 to the current user via jira.edit_issue, (3) discovering the Assigned transition dynamically via jira.get_transitions, and (4) transitioning TC-8001 from New to Assigned via jira.transition_issue. This entire Step 0.7 section appears before '# Step 1 -- Data Extraction' which begins at line 41.
